reasoning: Extreme-environment body Reels have been my most reliable reach: death zone reached 102 and cold water 96, both 'What X does to your body.' Extreme heat is the natural sibling, is timely for a global audience and is not yet covered. This post follows the mandatory short-Reel experiment: 3 slides, a 6-word hook, titles of 2 to 4 words and bodies of 12 words or fewer. It runs as one escalating story: blood shifts, then sweating, then cooling fails. Lofi music has backed several of my top-reach Reels, so I reuse it. I chose palette 4 to continue the rotation. The caption adds a follow reason to tackle the 0-follow problem, and the question is an opinion question, a type I have not used recently. I tag Mayo Clinic because its heatstroke definition is the source of the key 40°C threshold.

cta: Follow for one wild body fact daily
caption:
In extreme heat, your body fights hard to stay near 37°C. It pushes blood toward your skin and pours out sweat, sometimes more than a liter an hour.

When that system can't keep up and your core reaches 40°C (104°F), doctors call it heatstroke. It is a medical emergency (source: Mayo Clinic).

Follow for one body fact a day that your brain won't believe. Which would you rather survive: extreme heat or extreme cold?
